newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek govt says won't give in to farmers demands.
newsitem.headline: Greek govt says won't give in to farmers demands.

text.p: Greece's socialist government will not give in to demands by farmers who have blocked national roads for three weeks and its patience is wearing thin, National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou said on Tuesday.
"As far as the government is concerned our position is very clear. We shall not give in. There is no room for further concessions to farmers," he told Reuters Television in an interview.
Papandoniou said the government was deeply concerned about the farmers' barricades, which were crippling the economy.
"The consequences are quite substantial," he said. "The government is really very, very worried about the situation. Our our patience is wearing thin.
He hoped that on Thursday there would be a turning point in the confrontation after the farmers come to Athens for a protest rally.

He refused to be drawn on what action the government could take to get the farmers off the highways except to "stress that the government has the responsibility for the proper functioning of the country". --Deborah Kyvrikosaios, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
